notes: Machine-readable half of the rendered-composition contract. docs/visual/composition-principles.md is the prose half; where they disagree the ADR wins.
The collector emits composition-model/v1 JSON; the judge is a pure function over that model. Detection is structure/geometry only — never content strings, never personal data.
severity: blocking stops integration, warning feeds the L-C visual review as a required input, info is an observation with no verdict.
Every allowlist entry carries a reason and a signature set. An entry that waives nothing fails. Growing an allowlist is a contract change; shrinking it is the migration tickets' job.

routes[].heroMediaMinRatio: when set, the hero-rhythm section must dedicate at least this fraction of its area to media — catches media-bearing content rendered text-only (#1134). Per-item media mapping inside lists remains the portfolio obligation's data contract; the page-level aggregate is CL-6.

routes[].proseStackAllowed: exempts CL-11 for content-shaped pages whose body sections are long-form prose by design (markdown case studies). Requires the page to carry its composition elsewhere (hero media floor still applies via heroMediaMinRatio). Reason recorded per ADR-0023 exception policy — not a lint escape hatch: the flag is visible in review and must be justified in the route's contract entry.

routes[].proseSections: names the sections a content-shaped page may stack as prose. The exemption is scoped to those sections — the rest of the route (hero, media sections, any other block) is still judged by CL-11 (Issue #1149). The former page-wide `proseStackAllowed` flag is gone.

Issue #1149 — the model gained three per-section facts: `mediaByKind` (media area per element kind), `brokenMedia` (images that failed to load) and `repeatTailGapRatio` (how much of a repeated unit is empty below its content). CL-6 reads the first, CL-12 the third, CL-13 the second.

model.sections: document-order <section> elements; PageSection-derived ones carry data-tone / data-rhythm / data-section
model.signature: quantized composition vector: tone + column count + media presence + heading style + dominant block kinds. Component names are irrelevant; identical rendered structure yields identical signatures.

routes.label: portfolio detail (media-bearing slug ch4nge)
routes.proseSectionsReason: the markdown case-study body sections are long-form prose by design; the exemption applies to those sections only (Issue #1149)

rules.name: monotone-section-stack
rules.summary: Every section shares one tone and one composition signature — the page reads as an undifferentiated vertical stack.

detection.note: fires when ALL in-flow sections collapse to a single (tone, signature) pair

rules.exceptions: pages whose obligation IS a uniform index (e.g. a pure chronological list) may register a route-level exception with reason
rules.falsePositives: a deliberately austere monochrome page — mitigated by CL-8 staying warning-level and exceptions requiring a recorded reason

rules.name: repeated-section-structure
rules.summary: Three or more consecutive sections share an identical composition signature and the page shows no structural variation.

detection.note: repetition INSIDE one section (card grids, lists) is legitimate; this rule compares section-level signatures only

rules.exceptions: index routes where repetition is the content (activity timeline, links list) — route.indexRoute suppresses unless the run spans heterogeneous content types
rules.falsePositives: a page that genuinely has three same-shaped sections by meaning — requires exception entry

rules.name: missing-weight-hierarchy
rules.summary: No measurable difference in visual weight between primary and secondary content — everything competes equally.

detection.note: fires when max heading fontSize < fontRatioMin × median body fontSize AND no single block holds areaDominanceMin of content area AND surface contrast between sections is absent

rules.exceptions: tool/utility pages may declare reduced hierarchy expectations
rules.falsePositives: pages whose hierarchy is carried by tone rather than type scale — tone transitions count as hierarchy evidence

rules.name: unmotivated-narrow-column
rules.summary: On desktop the content column uses far less than the measure while large areas stay empty without breakout, media or a second column.

detection.note: contentWidthRatio is the union width of text-flow blocks over viewport width; emptyAreaRatio is the horizontal whitespace fraction of non-grid sections. Fires on a genuinely narrow text column, not on container padding.

rules.exceptions: intentional whitespace compositions (positive fixture) register a route or section exception
rules.falsePositives: editorial measure pages — the canonical 1024 container is itself the contract, so this rule measures blocks INSIDE sections that further narrow themselves

rules.name: uniform-grid-no-variation
rules.summary: A multi-column grid repeats equal tracks with no span/offset/breakout variation anywhere on the page.

detection.note: card indexes legitimately use equal tracks; the rule fires only when NO grid on the page shows intentional variation AND no Breakout/Overlap exists

rules.exceptions: dense index pages (portfolio grid) are expected-equal; declare per-route
rules.falsePositives: homogeneous data genuinely wants equal cells — warning level only

rules.name: media-neglect
rules.summary: A route declared mediaExpected renders little or no media area, or media-bearing items appear as text-only.

detection.note: ratio is media pixels over content pixels on routes flagged mediaExpected; text-only rendering of media-bearing items is reported per-item by the media usage contract (#1134)

rules.exceptions: routes may declare mediaExpected:false; items legitimately without assets are covered by the media manifest, not this rule
rules.falsePositives: a mediaExpected route in a data-empty state — the empty state itself is a separate contract

rules.name: mobile-naive-stack
rules.summary: Desktop multi-column composition collapses to an unmodified vertical stack on mobile — same order, same blocks, no recomposition.

detection.note: stacking IS the correct mobile transform; the defect is stacking with zero recomposition signals. Recomposition evidence: declared reorder/disclosure features, recompositionScore, or a >30% change in the (tone,rhythm) section order.

rules.exceptions: reading-order preservation is an accessibility requirement — reordering for effect must keep DOM order meaningful
rules.falsePositives: content that is legitimately sequential — warning level only

rules.name: zero-tone-variation
rules.summary: A page with four or more body sections uses no non-ground tone anywhere — surfaces carry no classification or emphasis.

detection.note: intentional monochrome is legitimate; this is a review prompt, not a defect verdict

rules.exceptions: route-level declaration for deliberately monochrome pages
rules.falsePositives: high — this is why it is warning-level

rules.name: no-focal-point
rules.summary: No block, display type size or surface contrast establishes a visual anchor — the eye has nowhere to land first.

detection.note: fires when no block holds dominantAreaMin of content area AND no font reaches displayFontRatioMin × body AND no tone/surface transition exists

rules.exceptions: utility pages (contact form, keyboard reference) may have diffuse hierarchy by nature
rules.falsePositives: pages whose focal point is an image measured under CL-6's mediaArea instead

rules.name: monotonous-lists
rules.summary: Multiple sections each render runs of near-identical units (cards, rows, tiles) and repetition DOMINATES the page — the 'same list stacked repeatedly' defect that reduces a page to a vertical stack of lists.

detection.note: repeatUnits counts sibling elements of near-identical geometry inside one section; the verdict requires repeater sections to dominate the page (>=50% of in-flow sections). Repetition inside ONE section is legitimate and never fires.

rules.exceptions: index routes are exempt (a catalog IS a list); a minority of list sections on a varied page is legitimate parallel structure; intentional repetition with variation is judged by the distinct-signature evidence in the detail string
rules.falsePositives: a page genuinely built from parallel catalogs — warning level feeds L-C review, never blocks

rules.name: stack-monotony
rules.summary: A run of consecutive sections that are all single-column, media-free, share the same content left edge and a similar density band — the page reduces to a left-aligned vertical stack regardless of which components produced it.

detection.note: signature-independent by design: different cards/lists/tiles that produce the same visual stack still count. Single-column prose is preserved when the run does not dominate the page or when sections vary axis/density/media. viewportMinWidth gates the rule to desktop: single-column stacking is the required mobile transform, not a defect.

rules.exceptions: index routes are exempt (catalogs stack by nature); intentional single-column editorial flows that vary density, axis or media do not form a qualifying run
rules.falsePositives: a genuinely minimal single-column page — mitigated by minRunLength + dominance; warning-level evidence is kept in the detail string

rules.name: empty-repeated-unit
rules.summary: A repeated card-shaped unit leaves the lower part of its own box empty — the content sits at the top of a plane the grid stretched.

detection.note: repeatTailGapRatio is the share of the repeated unit's HEIGHT that lies below its last content block — the question the eye asks ("is the bottom of this box empty?"). An area ratio was rejected: a list row is legitimately sparse, so the area ratio read every list as an empty card. The threshold is 0.5 — the bottom half of the unit is empty. Measured against the shipped pages: the portfolio card grid measured 0.52 while its cards were stretched, and 0.10 after the card stopped stretching; the home records measure 0.15 and the home status rows 0.02.

rules.exceptions: a unit whose emptiness IS the design (a spacer tile, a deliberately blank tile) has to be declared per route with a reason
rules.falsePositives: a unit whose content is painted as a background image or a canvas has no content block — such a unit must declare an exception

rules.name: broken-media
rules.summary: An image element failed to load, so the composition shows a broken frame where it promised media.

detection.note: the collector scrolls the document before measuring, so an image with a src and a zero intrinsic size after the settle is a failure, not a pending lazy load

rules.exceptions: an image that is intentionally a tracking pixel or a decorative spacer
rules.falsePositives: an image whose source is blocked by the capture environment (offline preview) — record it in the run report rather than silencing the rule

allowlistSchema.routeOrFile: route slug or source path the exception covers
allowlistSchema.reason: why the composition is legitimate despite the rule
allowlistSchema.signatures: optional set of section signatures the entry covers — an entry matching nothing is stale and fails
allowlistSchema.verification: how the exception was checked (fixture id, review doc, issue number)
